title: Select rows by position
summary: select makes a dataset containing chosen row positions. Positions begin at zero, and the requested order is preserved.
introduction: select makes a dataset containing chosen row positions. Positions begin at zero, and the requested order is preserved. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: select makes a dataset containing chosen row positions. Positions begin at zero, and the requested order is preserved.

blocks.code:
from datasets import Dataset
data = Dataset.from_dict({"text": ["moon", "sun", "stars"]})
small = data.select([2, 0])
print(list(small["text"]))
blocks.title: Select rows by position

blocks.text: The output is ['stars', 'moon']. Position 2 is selected first and position 0 second. The original dataset is still available.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A row position is not a permanent record ID if the data is reordered.
